headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill requires large energy users, such as data centers, to pay for the costs of increasing electric generating capacity, preventing these costs from being passed on to residential customers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, Senator Mark Warner, Governor Abigail Spanberger, House Democrats.
opponents: Data center industry (implied, as they would bear the costs).
news_headline: Virginia Shifts Data Center Energy Costs to Large Users
news_summary: Virginia's HB 1393 directs the primary electric provider to establish rates for large energy users (25 MW or more) to cover the costs of increased electric generating capacity. This measure aims to prevent these infrastructure costs from being passed on to residential customers, ensuring data centers pay their fair share.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water utilities report the total volume of potable and reclaimed water provided to data centers, increasing transparency on their water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups (e.g., Potomac Conservancy), local governments, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to reporting burden, though some utilities report it's not a major impact).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, SB 553, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, making these numbers publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency regarding the industry's water consumption, a growing concern for communities.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes new permit processes for high-energy data centers, mandating site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residences and schools, and allowing localities to require analysis of other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, environmental groups, local governments, Delegate Joshua Thomas, Senator Scott Surovell.
opponents: Data center industry, developers (due to increased regulatory burden and potential siting restrictions).
news_headline: New Virginia Law Mandates Data Center Noise Assessments
news_summary: Virginia's HB 153 establishes a new permit process for large data centers (100 MW or more), requiring developers to conduct site assessments for noise impacts on nearby residential areas and schools. This legislation empowers localities to demand further analysis of environmental impacts, addressing community concerns about data center sprawl.
